claims.text: Web Summit's organisers announced in September 2015 that the event would move from Dublin to Lisbon from 2016.
claims.quote: The Web Summit in Dublin will be no more from 2016 with the organisers confirming that the event is to up sticks and move to Lisbon

claims.text: The organisers cited infrastructure as one of their reasons for leaving Dublin (as Silicon Republic reports it).
claims.quote: with the organisation citing infrastructure as one of the reasons for its decision

claims.text: Founder Paddy Cosgrave said the move was made to take the next step in international growth.
claims.quote: We are going because we want to take the next step on our journey to international growth.

claims.text: The article reports a venue in Lisbon with capacity for more than 80,000 attendees, and expected more than 30,000 people at the 2015 edition in Dublin's RDS.
claims.quote: This November, the Web Summit expects more than 30,000 people to attend the event in the RDS.

claims.text: On the first Lisbon edition's opening night in 2016, ticket holders were left outside the venue.
claims.quote: People who paid thousands for tickets left waiting outside Web Summit

claims.text: TheJournal.ie reported that Web Summit's website confirmed the 2016 edition sold out, with 53,056 people attending.
claims.quote: The Web Summit website confirms that the event is sold out with 53,056 people attending.

claims.text: As TheJournal.ie recalls it, the organiser cited unreliable Wi-Fi at the RDS, traffic management, public transport and hotel costs as factors in leaving Dublin.
claims.quote: he cited unreliable WiFi at the RDS, issues with traffic management, public transport and hotel costs as influential factors

claims.text: In 2016 the late-late ticket prices ran from 1,000 euros (exhibition floor only) to 3,000 (General Attendee), 4,245 (Premium) and 5,245 (Platinum).
claims.quote: Late late ticket prices started at €1,000 for exhibition floor only and rose to €3,000 for a General Attendee, €4,245 for Premium and €5,245 for the Platinum ticket.

claims.text: In November 2017 Portugal's Prime Minister criticised a Web Summit dinner held at the National Pantheon in Lisbon as 'offensive'; the organiser apologised.
claims.quote: Paddy Cosgrave has apologised after Portugal’s Prime Minister criticised him for holding an “offensive” summit dinner at Lisbon’s National Pantheon

claims.text: The Prime Minister said laws would be amended to prevent the Pantheon being used for similar events (as TheJournal.ie reports it).
claims.quote: Laws will be amended to prevent the Pantheon from being used for similar events in the future, according to Costa
